title: Why Teotihuacan fell
summary: Teotihuacan's monuments were sacked and burned around 550 CE. Older invasion theories have given way to internal unrest and drought, two hypotheses that are not mutually exclusive.
why: A great city's ruling centre burned, possibly at the hands of its own people.

notes.problem: Source hedges: 'Some think' revolt; collapse 'might be related' to 535-536. Record stated both as fact.

question: What caused the fall of Teotihuacan, the great city of central Mexico?
evidence: Burning focused on ruling-class buildings with no clear signs of foreign invasion; juvenile skeletons show malnutrition; possible link to the 535–536 climate event.
wouldSettle: Precise dating of the burning set against climate records and evidence of who attacked elite buildings.

theories.name: Internal revolt
theories.idea: Civil strife and elite power struggles destroyed the ruling-class centre.

theories.name: Drought and famine
theories.idea: Climate stress, possibly the extreme weather of 535–536, caused crop failures and hunger.

theories.name: Foreign invasion
theories.idea: An earlier view that invaders destroyed the city, now less favoured.
